title: Feature registry frontmatter — the mint contract
$comment: Core half of the feature-frontmatter split (specfuse/specfuse#179, decided in #119). These are the fields the specs agent writes when it mints a feature or initiative registry entry, in the authoring plane; the constraints are taken unchanged from the orchestrator's feature-frontmatter.schema.json as of specfuse-orchestrator 0.6.0. Deliberately OPEN — no `additionalProperties: false` — because the orchestrator composes on top of this schema with `allOf` + `$ref` and closes the object itself with `unevaluatedProperties: false`; a closed base would reject the planning fields (`task_graph`, `feature_graph`, `next_step`) before the extension is consulted. Validated standalone, an unknown key therefore passes. Planning fields, their oneOf, and the state-conditional `next_step` requirement are the orchestrator's and are not declared here. The `$id` names core as the owner; the older core schemas still carry pre-extraction orchestrator `$id`s, which is a separate question.
description: YAML frontmatter a registry entry (`features/<id>.md`) carries from the moment it is minted: its correlation ID, lifecycle state, the repos it spans, and its autonomy default. A strict weakening of the orchestrator's feature-frontmatter schema: anything valid there is valid here.

correlation_id.description: Feature- or initiative-level correlation ID: FEAT-YYYY-NNNN (legacy feature) or INIT-YYYY-NNNN (initiative). Sub-unit IDs (TNN/FNN) are not valid here. Format and minting rules: rules/correlation-ids.md.

state.description: Lifecycle state from the shared spine in glossary.md §"Lifecycle states" (initiative / feature level).

involved_repos.description: Component repositories the feature or initiative spans, as `owner/repo` strings.
